subject: Polity
topic: Money bill and finance bill — mixed tiers
description: Article 110, Speaker's role, Rajya Sabha limits, financial bill vs money bill

questions.stem: A Money Bill is defined in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 110 — exhaustive definition. A bill is a Money Bill only if it contains provisions dealing exclusively with any of seven specified matters — imposition/abolition of a tax, borrowing of money, Consolidated Fund / Contingency Fund, appropriation from Consolidated Fund, declaring an expenditure 'charged' on CFI, receipts/audit of public accounts, or any matter incidental to these. Article 108 is joint sitting; Article 112 is Annual Financial Statement; Article 117 is Financial Bills.

questions.stem: The final authority to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill rests with the:
questions.explanation: Article 110(3) — 'the decision of the Speaker of the House of the People thereon shall be final.' The Speaker's endorsement on every Money Bill certifies its status; Rajya Sabha cannot question the certificate. The Supreme Court in Rojer Mathew (2019) held that judicial review of the Speaker's certification is possible but has never overturned one. A Money Bill originates only in Lok Sabha with prior recommendation of the President.

questions.stem: Under Article 109, Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill with or without its recommendations within how many days from receipt?
questions.explanation: Article 109(4) — if Rajya Sabha does not return the Money Bill within 14 days, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses at the end of the 14-day period in the form passed by Lok Sabha. Lok Sabha can accept or reject any of Rajya Sabha's recommendations — there is no joint-sitting provision for Money Bills. The 14-day clock is constitutionally fixed; it cannot be extended.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature that distinguishes a Money Bill from an ordinary bill?

options.option_text: Requires prior recommendation of the President
Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations, not amendments
Joint sitting can be convened if disagreement arises

questions.explanation: Article 108 (joint sitting) does NOT apply to Money Bills — because there can be no disagreement. If Rajya Sabha rejects or delays, the bill is deemed passed after 14 days anyway. Joint sittings have happened only 3 times in Indian history (Dowry Prohibition 1961, Banking Services Commission 1978, POTA 2002) — all ordinary bills. A, B and C are all distinguishing features of Money Bills.

questions.stem: A 'Financial Bill' under Article 117(1) differs from a Money Bill because a Financial Bill:

options.option_text: Contains matters beyond Article 110 but also includes matters under Article 110
Can only be introduced in Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Three-fold classification: Money Bill (Art 110) — exclusively A110 matters; Financial Bill Category I (Art 117(1)) — contains A110 matters plus other provisions; Financial Bill Category II (Art 117(3)) — involves expenditure from CFI but no A110 matters. A and B require President's recommendation to introduce; only C does not. Rajya Sabha has full powers over Financial Bills (including joint sitting possible) — unlike Money Bills.

questions.stem: The Aadhaar Act 2016 was passed as a Money Bill. The Supreme Court's majority view in Puttaswamy (2018) / K.S. Puttaswamy (Aadhaar) was:

options.option_text: Certification as Money Bill was unconstitutional
Certification was valid; the Aadhaar scheme was constitutional
Aadhaar itself was struck down entirely
The Speaker must always consult President

questions.explanation: In K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (26 Sep 2018), the 5-judge bench by 4:1 upheld Aadhaar Act's passage as a Money Bill — Section 7 (targeted delivery of subsidies from Consolidated Fund) was held to be the bill's core purpose. Justice Chandrachud dissented. In Rojer Mathew (2019) a 5-judge bench referred the Money Bill question to a 7-judge bench; decision still pending. Aadhaar scheme itself was upheld except Sections 33(2), 47, 57.

questions.stem: The Union Budget, placed before Parliament each year, is technically called the:
questions.explanation: Article 112 — the 'Annual Financial Statement' (AFS) is the document of estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for a financial year. Popularly called 'the Budget'. The Finance Bill (Art 117) implements taxation proposals; the Appropriation Bill (Art 114) authorises withdrawal from CFI. Both are typically certified as Money Bills. Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget from 2017-18.
